## Description

The most abundant white blood cell (~8 µm round, ~330 µm³; ~15 × 8 µm when migrating). It does not
divide; it lives hours and dies by apoptosis without inflaming. It follows the formylated peptides of
bacteria (fMLP), engulfs them and digests them. It also phagocytoses sperm (in semen with leukocytes
and in the female tract; immotile ones, which cannot escape, are the ones caught).

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: not seeded in the default drops (inoculate it from the Catalogue).

Prepared plates: `blood_smear`, `semen_leukocytes`.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

A crawling [animal cell](../../mechanics/animal-cells.md#neutrophil) with fMLP chemotaxis and a phagocytic cup;
almost entirely glycolytic. Validated: migration speed in an fMLP gradient. Appears in the cell
culture, the blood smear and `semen_leukocytes`.

## Literature

- Zigmond S.H. (1977) Ability of polymorphonuclear leukocytes to orient in gradients of chemotactic
  factors. J. Cell Biol. 75: 606–616 (~10–20 µm/min in fMLP).
- Carruthers A. (1990) Facilitated diffusion of glucose. Physiol. Rev. 70: 1135–1176 (GLUT1 Km ~1–3 mM).

## Not implemented yet

- No NETs, degranulation or respiratory burst.
- No chemotactic index validation (roadmap: experiment 49).

## Unique and shared mechanics

Shares the [phagocytic cup](../../mechanics/feeding-and-phagocytosis.md) with the amoebae and fMLP chemotaxis is
unique to it.
